stories.new_fact: The FCC advanced for public comment a request that could allow political groups to use artificial or prerecorded voices in unsolicited wireless calls before the midterms.
stories.new_takeaway: The practical risk is a compressed election-operations test of consent rules, carrier response and misinformation enforcement, not simply a new AI-call anecdote.
stories.why_now: AP reported the FCC action on October 7 and said the commission could rule as soon as late October.
stories.previous_coverage: The October 7 episode covered ABC's FCC license-review lawsuit; this is a different FCC operating question about campaign robocall consent and AI voices.
stories.uncertainty: The FCC may grant, narrow or reject the waiver; existing deception and voter-intimidation laws may still apply.
stories.watch: Whether the FCC grants, narrows or delays the waiver before late October.

stories.new_fact: Columbus opened applications through October 23 for the inaugural 15-member Community Crisis Response Advisory Board.
stories.new_takeaway: The voter-approved non-police crisis program is moving from mandate to implementation design, where dispatch scope and oversight will matter.
stories.why_now: Applications opened October 6 and were reported October 7, with appointments planned for early November.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent Columbus segments covered gas-tax relief, early voting, waterline work and public-safety adjacent flyer response; this specific implementation step was not covered.
stories.uncertainty: The board's membership and practical authority are not yet known.
stories.watch: Who is appointed after the October 23 application deadline and whether the first meeting occurs by the end of November.

stories.new_fact: Fannie Mae updated VOE method flexibility, K-1 income verification, income continuance, employment-offer documentation, AOL eligibility and seller wire-instruction submission.
stories.new_takeaway: The consequence is operational: underwriters, closers and secondary teams need updated checklists and permissions before post-closing defects appear.
stories.why_now: The Selling Guide announcement is dated October 7, and several changes are effective immediately.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior week focused on UAD exceptions, Freddie delivery and income calculator changes, credit-score pricing and mortgage rates; this is a separate selling-guide workflow update.
stories.uncertainty: Investor overlays, local attorney-title acceptance and lender-specific wire controls may limit immediate use.
stories.watch: Whether lenders publish internal bulletins updating VOE, K-1, AOL and Form 482 controls.

stories.new_fact: Plaid introduced Instant Link, LendScore 2, specialized lending models including home lending, Signal 4 and a fraud foundation model with vendor-reported internal evaluation lifts.
stories.new_takeaway: For banks, the decision is not whether the vendor numbers sound attractive; it is whether challenger tests prove credit, ACH and fraud lift without fair-lending or false-positive damage.
stories.why_now: Plaid published the model updates on October 6, within the 48-hour window for the October 8 episode.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent bank-AI segments covered Incognia, Upstart, Mastercard agent-payment trust tools, Kyndryl/BIL, Barclays and Feedzai; Plaid's new model family was not covered.
stories.uncertainty: The numbers are company claims from Plaid tests, not independent lender portfolio outcomes.
stories.watch: Whether a named lender publishes live portfolio results for the new Plaid cash-flow, ACH or fraud models.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Plaid / lanes 2 and 3 / new announced row for credit scoring, ACH payment-risk scoring and fraud foundation model; evidence rank company claim with internal evaluation metrics.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI rolled GPT-6 into ChatGPT with Intelligent UI and published a deployment-safety card for October GPT-6 Sol and Luna.
stories.new_takeaway: The workflow implication is that generated interfaces now need validation alongside generated text, especially in regulated environments.
stories.why_now: OpenAI published the product update and safety card on October 7.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent frontier segments covered Anthropic cyber access, GPT-Rosalind pricing, federal AI task force, autonomous agent probing and prior OpenAI release notes; Intelligent UI was not covered.
stories.uncertainty: The reported metrics are OpenAI internal evaluations, and enterprise outcomes have not been independently replicated.
stories.watch: Whether OpenAI or outside evaluators publish task-level evidence on generated-interface correctness, accessibility, logging or safety.
stories.frontier_bar: Agent and tool-use/access shift with lab-reported safety evaluation; GPT-6 can generate interactive components and task-specific tools inside ChatGPT.

stories.new_fact: AP reported the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%, the Dow fell 341 points, the Nasdaq fell 0.2%, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.36% before easing.
stories.new_takeaway: The market implication for lenders and local finance is that record equity optimism remains vulnerable to the financing cost and energy-price test.
stories.why_now: The market move occurred Wednesday, October 7.
stories.previous_coverage: Markets have been compactly covered all week; this update is fresh and tied to rates, oil and borrowing costs rather than a scoreboard recap.
stories.uncertainty: The next test is whether earnings growth and Treasury demand absorb high yields.
stories.watch: Whether 10-year yields stay near the 5.3% area and whether Brent remains near $100.

stories.new_fact: The Columbus forecast showed a sunny, warm Thursday, partly cloudy Thursday night and higher rain chances over the weekend.
stories.new_takeaway: Use Thursday and Friday for outdoor plans before the wetter weekend signal.
stories.why_now: Daily Columbus weather is included for practical planning.
stories.previous_coverage: Weather is routine and compact; no major advisory was carried over.
stories.watch: Saturday afternoon and Sunday shower timing.
